# darts-duel-program-standard

| | |
|---|---|
| Benchmark | Embodied Agent Olympiad |
| Mode | standard (`eai-standard-turn/1.0`) |
| Twin | — (standard only: Olympiad sports have no privileged twin) |
| Simulator / robot | `analytic dart flight (RK4, gravity + quadratic drag, darts.py) with a MuJoCo scene for the cameras` / `none` |
| Family / instance | `darts_duel` |
| Oracle | `full` — solution/: the sport's reference player (camera images and /spec only); tools/check runs it live and it wins the default configuration |
| Agent time budget | 7200 s; tokens: protocol default (PROTOCOL §5) |
| Base image | `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/eai-olympiad:0.1.0` |

## Task
Best of 3 legs of 501 double-out at a regulation board, each dart a release command (yaw, pitch, speed) with seeded scatter under gravity and quadratic drag; format 501: you against a built-in scripted thrower (opponent level 1-4, `game spec` opponent), format duel: two players at one board; format `duel` (seats A, B),
action level `low`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/darts/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions) and the first player (`FIRST_PLAYER`; play both orders).

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [WDF Playing and Tournament Rules, 20th revised edition](https://dartswdf.com/storage/uploads/fb05b306-c92c-4f08-b512-affb092a1b3d/2018-02-28_WDF_Playing_and_Tournament_Rules_rev20.pdf) version 2018 |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | WDF 1.02, 13.01 | the darts are thrown by a release mechanism with a stated scatter, not by hand, and there are no practice darts |
| D2 | WDF 1.05-1.06, 3.02-3.03 | darts always stick where the point reaches the board: no bounce-outs, fall-outs or wire deflections |
| D3 | WDF 12.01-12.03 | the throw order is fixed instead of a throw for the bull: in format 501 the opponent throws first in legs 1 and 3; in the duel the configured first player (`game spec` first_player) throws first in legs 1 and 3, and both orders are played |
| D4 | WDF 12 (play continues until a player checks out) | a cost limit: a leg nobody has checked out after 30 visits each goes to the lower remaining score; if level, to the player with more chess-clock time left (the scripted opponent uses no clock time, so it wins a level leg); if the clocks are level too, to the player who did not start the leg |
| D5 | WDF 1.02 (the darts are thrown by hand) | the release mechanism (D1) is declared at a human elite throw, not a machine's: release speed 5 to 7 m/s, an estimate (no dart-throwing robot publishes its release speed; a skilled thrower releases at about 5.1 to 5.5 m/s, e.g. arXiv:2604.01130, https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01130, after Venkadesan et al.); until darts-5: 4 to 9 m/s, where 9 m/s is far beyond a human throw and below about 5 m/s no dart reaches the top of the board at all. The cap holds for the commanded speed, the executed one scatters around it; the execution scatter is an estimate too |
